1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# adopt.sh -- idempotently inject the dwarves-kit operate-contract into a target repo.
3	#
4	# Adoption = the per-repo trigger that makes an agent classify + pick a lane and that makes the
5	# ship-gate engage. It injects the CONTRACT + a proof marker + pointers; it never copies the
6	# engine (lib/, the full WORKFLOW matrix) -- the gate machinery reads those from the install
7	# ($KIT_ROOT). Non-destructive: AGENTS.md + the proof marker are never overwritten.
8	#
9	# The CLAUDE.md loader uses an `@AGENTS.md` import (Claude Code includes the file, not just a
10	# "go read it" pointer; absorbed from repository-harness's --claude shim).
11	#
12	# Usage: adopt.sh [--check | --dry-run | --refresh] [--with <a,b,c>] <target-dir>
13	#   --check   : report status only (exit 0 adopted / 1 not), write nothing.
14	#   --dry-run : print what would change, write nothing.
15	#   --refresh : re-sync the kit-managed pieces (WORKFLOW pointer + the CLAUDE.md loader block)
16	#               to their current form. AGENTS.md + the proof marker are still never overwritten.
17	#   --with <a,b,c> : only meaningful the first time (seeding a fresh <target>/.kit.toml): the
18	#               named modules start `true` in the seeded [modules] section instead of the
19	#               kit-root defaults. Ignored (with a note) once <target>/.kit.toml exists -- a
20	#               project's own config is never overwritten by re-running adopt (SPEC-192).
21	#
22	# Per-project override close-out (SPEC-192, goal 06): the resolver (lib/config/kit-config.sh,
23	# goal 01) already merges <target>/.kit.toml over the kit-root default. This closes the loop:
24	# adopt seeds a starter <target>/.kit.toml (opt-in; never overwritten after creation) and, on
25	# EVERY run (fresh or --refresh), wires the currently-enabled HOOK-bearing modules (board,
26	# session, advisor, cosmetic) into <target>/.claude/settings.json via a jq MERGE (never a
27	# wholesale file rewrite -- other entries in that file are preserved). Command/skill modules
28	# (queue, stats, quiz_gate, weekend_batch, bridge) need no settings.json entry, so they are
29	# recorded in .kit.toml but never touch settings.json. This is "wired at adopt time", not read
30	# per hook fire: re-running adopt.sh (an explicit, deliberate action) recomputes the project's
31	# wired set from its CURRENT .kit.toml; nothing reads .kit.toml at hook-fire time.
32	set -uo pipefail
33	
34	KIT_ROOT="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-$HOME/.claude/dwarves-kit}"
35	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
36	SRC_ROOT="$(cd "$SELF_DIR/.." && pwd)"   # the dwarves-kit repo root when run from its lib/
37	START="<!-- kit:adopt -->"               # managed-block markers in the consumer CLAUDE.md
38	END="<!-- /kit:adopt -->"
39	
40	tmp=""                                   # scratch file; the trap cleans it up on any early exit
41	trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
42	
43	usage() { echo "usage: adopt.sh [--check | --dry-run | --refresh] [--with <a,b,c>] [--] <target-dir>" >&2; exit 64; }
44	
45	CHECK=0 DRY=0 REFRESH=0 WITH_ARG=""
46	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
47	  case "$1" in
48	    --check) CHECK=1; shift;;
49	    --dry-run) DRY=1; shift;;
50	    --refresh) REFRESH=1; shift;;
51	    --with) shift; WITH_ARG="${1:-}"; shift;;
52	    --with=*) WITH_ARG="${1#--with=}"; shift;;
53	    --) shift; break;;
54	    -*) usage;;
55	    *) break;;
56	  esac
57	done
58	TARGET="${1:-}"; [ -n "$TARGET" ] || usage
59	[ -d "$TARGET" ] || { echo "adopt: target dir not found: $TARGET" >&2; exit 1; }
60	
61	agents="$TARGET/AGENTS.md"
62	workflow="$TARGET/WORKFLOW.md"
63	claude="$TARGET/CLAUDE.md"
64	marker="$TARGET/docs/verification/README.md"
65	dotkit="$TARGET/.kit.toml"
66	project_settings="$TARGET/.claude/settings.json"
67	
68	is_adopted() {
69	  # -qxF: the marker must be its own full line (matches how awk strips the block). A substring
70	  # grep would mis-detect a marker quoted inside prose and skip the append path (review #6).
71	  [ -f "$agents" ] && [ -f "$marker" ] && [ -f "$claude" ] \
72	    && grep -qxF "$START" "$claude" 2>/dev/null
73	}
74	
75	if [ "$CHECK" -eq 1 ]; then
76	  is_adopted && { echo "adopted: $TARGET"; exit 0; } || { echo "not adopted: $TARGET"; exit 1; }
77	fi
78	
79	git -C "$TARGET" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 \
80	  || echo "adopt: warning: $TARGET is not a git repo (adopting at filesystem level anyway)" >&2
81	
82	# Resolve a source AGENTS.md: the kit repo (dev) first, then the install.
83	src_agents=""
84	for c in "$SRC_ROOT/AGENTS.md" "$KIT_ROOT/AGENTS.md"; do
85	  [ -f "$c" ] && { src_agents="$c"; break; }
86	done
87	[ -n "$src_agents" ] || { echo "adopt: no source AGENTS.md (looked in $SRC_ROOT, $KIT_ROOT)" >&2; exit 1; }
88	
89	workflow_block() {
90	  cat <<EOF
91	# WORKFLOW.md (pointer)
92	
93	This repo is adopted into the dwarves-kit. The canonical lanes and the lane x phase gate matrix
94	live in the installed kit: \`$KIT_ROOT/WORKFLOW.md\`. Read that for the lanes and the gate at each
95	phase boundary. The gate machinery (gate-ledger, ship-gate) parses that copy, not this file.
96	EOF
97	}
98	
99	claude_block() {
100	  printf '%s\n' "$START"
101	  printf '## Operating layer (dwarves-kit)\n\n'
102	  printf '@AGENTS.md\n\n'
103	  printf 'Before touching code, classify the lane: `bash %s/bin/classify lane classify "<task>"`.\n' "$KIT_ROOT"
104	  printf 'A full-lane change records its gates via `%s/bin/gate ledger` or the ship-gate blocks the push.\n' "$KIT_ROOT"
105	  printf '%s\n' "$END"
106	}
107	
108	did=0
109	note() { echo "adopt: would $*"; }
110	
111	# 1. AGENTS.md -- the operate-contract. NEVER overwritten (even on --refresh).
112	if [ ! -f "$agents" ]; then
113	  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "create AGENTS.md (from $src_agents)"; else cp "$src_agents" "$agents"; fi
114	  did=1
115	fi
116	
117	# 2. WORKFLOW.md pointer -- create if absent; --refresh overwrites to current. Write atomically
118	# (tmp + mv) so a kill / full disk mid-write can't leave a half-written pointer (review #3).
119	if [ ! -f "$workflow" ] || { [ "$REFRESH" -eq 1 ] && ! cmp -s <(workflow_block) "$workflow"; }; then
120	  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "write WORKFLOW.md pointer"; else
121	    tmp="$(mktemp)"; workflow_block > "$tmp"; mv "$tmp" "$workflow"
122	  fi
123	  did=1
124	fi
125	
126	# 3. CLAUDE.md loader (@AGENTS.md import) -- append once; --refresh replaces the managed block.
127	if [ ! -f "$claude" ] || ! grep -qxF "$START" "$claude" 2>/dev/null; then
128	  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "append the CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md loader block"; else
129	    tmp="$(mktemp)"; { [ -f "$claude" ] && cat "$claude"; printf '\n'; claude_block; } > "$tmp"; mv "$tmp" "$claude"
130	  fi
131	  did=1
132	elif [ "$REFRESH" -eq 1 ]; then
133	  # Refuse to refresh a block with a START but no END: the awk strip would drop everything from
134	  # START to EOF and mv would install the truncated file (silent data loss; review CRITICAL #1).
135	  # This is exactly the legacy single-sentinel shape, so the operator migrates it by hand.
136	  if ! grep -qxF "$END" "$claude" 2>/dev/null; then
137	    echo "adopt: $claude has '$START' but no '$END' line; refusing --refresh (would truncate)." >&2
138	    echo "adopt: add an '$END' line after the managed block, or delete the block, then re-run." >&2
139	    exit 1
140	  fi
141	  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "refresh the CLAUDE.md loader block"; did=1; else
142	    tmp="$(mktemp)"
143	    # END{if(drop)exit 3}: belt-and-suspenders against an unterminated block slipping past the
144	    # guard above; the `|| exit` stops us from mv-ing a truncated file when awk bails.
145	    awk -v s="$START" -v e="$END" '
146	      $0==s{drop=1; next} drop&&$0==e{drop=0; next} !drop{print}
147	      END{if(drop) exit 3}' "$claude" > "$tmp" \
148	      || { echo "adopt: failed to strip the managed block from $claude (unterminated?)" >&2; exit 1; }
149	    claude_block >> "$tmp"
150	    if cmp -s "$tmp" "$claude"; then rm -f "$tmp"; else mv "$tmp" "$claude"; did=1; fi
151	  fi
152	fi
153	
154	# 4. proof marker -- presence opts this repo into the ship-gate. NEVER overwritten.
155	if [ ! -f "$marker" ]; then
156	  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "create docs/verification/README.md (proof marker)"; else
157	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$marker")"
158	    cat > "$marker" <<EOF
159	# Verification (proof-of-done marker)
160	
161	Presence of this file opts this repo into the dwarves-kit proof-of-done ship-gate. A
162	behavioral/stateful change owes a recorded run here; the shape per loop type comes from the
163	install: \`bash $KIT_ROOT/lib/gate/proof-gate.sh contract "<task>"\`.
164	EOF
165	  fi
166	  did=1
167	fi
168	
169	# --- SPEC-192 (goal 06): close the per-project override loop -----------------------------
170	
171	# Resolve the kit-root kit.toml (dev checkout first, then the install) -- same lookup shape
172	# as src_agents above.
173	kit_root_toml=""
174	for c in "$SRC_ROOT/kit.toml" "$KIT_ROOT/kit.toml"; do
175	  [ -f "$c" ] && { kit_root_toml="$c"; break; }
176	done
177	
178	# module -> its hook script basenames (space-separated; empty = hookless -- queue, stats,
179	# quiz_gate, weekend_batch, bridge are commands/skills with no hook to gate). Kept in sync
180	# with install.sh's kit_module_hooks() (same doc note there): only board/session/advisor/
181	# cosmetic carry a hook, so only those need a settings.json entry.
182	kit_module_hooks() {
183	  case "$1" in
184	    board) echo "backlog-stage.sh" ;;
185	    session) echo "context-readiness.sh output-offload.sh pre-compact-backup.sh post-compact-reinject.sh session-state-save.sh harvest.sh citation-guard.sh" ;;
186	    advisor) echo "context-hints.sh" ;;
187	    cosmetic) echo "auto-format.sh notification.sh slop-cleaner.sh statusline.sh codebase-index.sh permission-auto-approve.sh" ;;
188	    *) echo "" ;;
189	  esac
190	}
191	
192	KIT_KNOWN_MODULES="board session advisor cosmetic queue stats quiz_gate weekend_batch bridge"
193	
194	# Load the config resolver in a function scope so its own `${1:-}` selftest check (see
195	# lib/config/kit-config.sh) never sees adopt.sh's own positional parameters (TARGET etc).
196	_kit_load_config_resolver() {
197	  # shellcheck source=lib/config/kit-config.sh
198	  source "$SELF_DIR/config/kit-config.sh"
199	}
200	RESOLVER_OK=1
201	_kit_load_config_resolver 2>/dev/null || RESOLVER_OK=0
202	
203	# 5. Per-project .kit.toml -- an OPT-IN starter (SPEC-192). Created only if absent; a
204	# project's own config is NEVER overwritten by adopt, fresh or --refresh (same invariant as
205	# AGENTS.md / the proof marker). --with (first run only) seeds the named modules `true`;
206	# every other key seeds the kit-root default it would inherit anyway -- writing the line
207	# explicitly just makes the override point visible and editable.
208	if [ -n "$kit_root_toml" ] && [ "$RESOLVER_OK" -eq 1 ]; then
209	  if [ ! -f "$dotkit" ]; then
210	    if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then
211	      note "seed a starter .kit.toml (modules: ${WITH_ARG:-kit-root defaults})"
212	    else
213	      with_norm=""
214	      [ -n "$WITH_ARG" ] && with_norm=" $(echo "$WITH_ARG" | tr ',' ' ' | xargs) "
215	      tmp="$(mktemp)"
216	      {
217	        echo "# .kit.toml -- this PROJECT's override of the kit-root defaults (SPEC-192)."
218	        echo "# Only the keys you set here matter; every key you omit inherits the kit-root"
219	        echo "# default at $KIT_ROOT/kit.toml (lib/config/kit-config.sh: project keys WIN)."
220	        echo "# Re-run \`bash $KIT_ROOT/lib/adopt.sh --refresh <this repo>\` (or /kit:adopt) after"
221	        echo "# editing [modules] to re-wire this project's .claude/settings.json to match --"
222	        echo "# adopt reads this file at adopt time; no hook reads it at hook-fire time."
223	        echo ""
224	        echo "[modules]"
225	        for m in $KIT_KNOWN_MODULES; do
226	          if [ -n "$with_norm" ]; then
227	            case "$with_norm" in *" $m "*) v=true ;; *) v=false ;; esac
228	          else
229	            KIT_CONFIG_ROOT="$(dirname "$kit_root_toml")" KIT_PROJECT_ROOT="$TARGET" \
230	              v="$(kit_config_get "modules.$m" "false")"
231	          fi
232	          echo "$m = $v"
233	        done
234	      } > "$tmp"
235	      mv "$tmp" "$dotkit"
236	    fi
237	    did=1
238	  elif [ -n "$WITH_ARG" ]; then
239	    echo "adopt: note: $dotkit already exists; --with ignored (edit the file's [modules] section directly)" >&2
240	  fi
241	fi
242	
243	# 6. Per-project hook-module wiring into <target>/.claude/settings.json (SPEC-192). Runs on
244	# EVERY adopt invocation (fresh or --refresh), reading this project's CURRENT .kit.toml (project
245	# override, else the kit-root default -- the resolver from goal 01), so a hand-edited .kit.toml
246	# is picked up the next time adopt runs. Never on hook-fire (Not: runtime per-call module
247	# toggling). A jq MERGE, never a settings.json rewrite: only kit-module hook entries
248	# (dwarves-kit/hooks/*) are added/removed; every other entry in the file is preserved untouched.
249	# Command/skill modules (queue, stats, quiz_gate, weekend_batch, bridge) have no hook, so they
250	# never touch settings.json regardless of their .kit.toml value.
251	if [ -n "$kit_root_toml" ] && [ "$RESOLVER_OK" -eq 1 ] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
252	  settings_src=""
253	  for c in "$SRC_ROOT/settings.json" "$KIT_ROOT/settings.json"; do
254	    [ -f "$c" ] && { settings_src="$c"; break; }
255	  done
256	  if [ -n "$settings_src" ]; then
257	    HOOKED_MODULES="board session advisor cosmetic"
258	    enabled_list="" wired_hook_names=""
259	    for m in $HOOKED_MODULES; do
260	      KIT_CONFIG_ROOT="$(dirname "$kit_root_toml")" KIT_PROJECT_ROOT="$TARGET" \
261	        v="$(kit_config_get "modules.$m" "false")"
262	      if [ "$v" = "true" ]; then
263	        enabled_list="$enabled_list $m"
264	        wired_hook_names="$wired_hook_names $(kit_module_hooks "$m")"
265	      fi
266	    done
267	    wired_hook_names="$(echo "$wired_hook_names" | xargs)"
268	
269	    hook_re=""
270	    for h in $wired_hook_names; do
271	      esc="$(printf '%s' "$h" | sed 's/\./\\./g')"
272	      if [ -z "$hook_re" ]; then hook_re="$esc"; else hook_re="$hook_re|$esc"; fi
273	    done
274	
275	    if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then
276	      note "wire $project_settings for modules:${enabled_list:-<none>} (hooks:${wired_hook_names:-none})"
277	    else
278	      before_wired=""
279	      [ -f "$project_settings" ] && before_wired="$(jq -r '[.hooks // {} | to_entries[]? | .value[]? | .hooks[]? | .command] | .[]' "$project_settings" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'dwarves-kit/hooks/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.sh' | sort -u)"
280	
281	      filtered="$(mktemp)"
282	      if [ -n "$hook_re" ]; then
283	        jq --arg re "$hook_re" '
284	          .hooks |= (
285	            to_entries | map(
286	              .value |= (
287	                map(.hooks |= map(select(.command | test($re)))) | map(select(.hooks | length > 0))
288	              )
289	            ) | from_entries
290	          )
291	        ' "$settings_src" > "$filtered" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"hooks":{}}' > "$filtered"
292	      else
293	        echo '{"hooks":{}}' > "$filtered"
294	      fi
295	
296	      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$project_settings")"
297	      # One code path for both "no project settings.json yet" and "re-wiring an existing
298	      # one" (a missing file reads as {}): strip any prior kit-module hook (dwarves-kit/
299	      # hooks/*, added by an earlier adopt run), then union in the currently-enabled set.
300	      # Canonicalized (jq -S, arrays sorted by their own JSON text) so a re-run over an
301	      # UNCHANGED .kit.toml reproduces byte-identical output -- adopt's own idempotency
302	      # invariant (test-adopt.sh), not just "the same hook names, any order".
303	      existing_json='{}'
304	      [ -f "$project_settings" ] && existing_json="$(cat "$project_settings")"
305	      merged="$(jq -n --argjson existing "$existing_json" --slurpfile kit "$filtered" '
306	        $existing as $ex | ($kit[0].hooks // {}) as $kh
307	        | $ex
308	        | .hooks = (
309	            ((($ex.hooks // {}) | to_entries
310	              | map(.value |= (
311	                  map(.hooks |= map(select(.command | tostring | contains("dwarves-kit/hooks/") | not)))
312	                  | map(select(.hooks | length > 0))
313	                ))
314	             ) + ($kh | to_entries))
315	            | group_by(.key)
316	            | map({
317	                key: .[0].key,
318	                value: ([.[].value[]] | unique_by(tostring) | sort_by(tostring))
319	              })
320	            | sort_by(.key)
321	            | from_entries
322	          )
323	      ' 2>/dev/null)"
324	      if [ -n "$merged" ] && echo "$merged" | jq -S '.' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
325	        echo "$merged" | jq -S '.' > "$project_settings"
326	      else
327	        echo "adopt: warning: jq merge of $project_settings failed; left untouched" >&2
328	      fi
329	      rm -f "$filtered"
330	
331	      after_wired=""
332	      [ -f "$project_settings" ] && after_wired="$(jq -r '[.hooks // {} | to_entries[]? | .value[]? | .hooks[]? | .command] | .[]' "$project_settings" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'dwarves-kit/hooks/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.sh' | sort -u)"
333	      [ "$before_wired" != "$after_wired" ] && did=1
334	      echo "adopt: project hook-module wiring for $TARGET -> modules:${enabled_list:-<none>}"
335	    fi
336	  fi
337	fi
338	
339	if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then
340	  echo "adopt: --dry-run for $TARGET ($([ "$did" -eq 1 ] && echo 'changes above' || echo 'already adopted, nothing to do'))"
341	else
342	  echo "adopt: $TARGET ($([ "$did" -eq 1 ] && echo updated || echo 'already adopted, no-op'))"
343	fi
344

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# adopt.sh -- idempotently inject the dwarves-kit operate-contract into a target repo.
#
# Adoption = the per-repo trigger that makes an agent classify + pick a lane and that makes the
# ship-gate engage. It injects the CONTRACT + a proof marker + pointers; it never copies the
# engine (lib/, the full WORKFLOW matrix) -- the gate machinery reads those from the install
# ($KIT_ROOT). Non-destructive: AGENTS.md + the proof marker are never overwritten.
#
# The CLAUDE.md loader uses an `@AGENTS.md` import (Claude Code includes the file, not just a
# "go read it" pointer; absorbed from repository-harness's --claude shim).
#
# Usage: adopt.sh [--check | --dry-run | --refresh] [--with <a,b,c>] <target-dir>
#   --check   : report status only (exit 0 adopted / 1 not), write nothing.
#   --dry-run : print what would change, write nothing.
#   --refresh : re-sync the kit-managed pieces (WORKFLOW pointer + the CLAUDE.md loader block)
#               to their current form. AGENTS.md + the proof marker are still never overwritten.
#   --with <a,b,c> : only meaningful the first time (seeding a fresh <target>/.kit.toml): the
#               named modules start `true` in the seeded [modules] section instead of the
#               kit-root defaults. Ignored (with a note) once <target>/.kit.toml exists -- a
#               project's own config is never overwritten by re-running adopt (SPEC-192).
#
# Per-project override close-out (SPEC-192, goal 06): the resolver (lib/config/kit-config.sh,
# goal 01) already merges <target>/.kit.toml over the kit-root default. This closes the loop:
# adopt seeds a starter <target>/.kit.toml (opt-in; never overwritten after creation) and, on
# EVERY run (fresh or --refresh), wires the currently-enabled HOOK-bearing modules (board,
# session, advisor, cosmetic) into <target>/.claude/settings.json via a jq MERGE (never a
# wholesale file rewrite -- other entries in that file are preserved). Command/skill modules
# (queue, stats, quiz_gate, weekend_batch, bridge) need no settings.json entry, so they are
# recorded in .kit.toml but never touch settings.json. This is "wired at adopt time", not read
# per hook fire: re-running adopt.sh (an explicit, deliberate action) recomputes the project's
# wired set from its CURRENT .kit.toml; nothing reads .kit.toml at hook-fire time.
set -uo pipefail

KIT_ROOT="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-$HOME/.claude/dwarves-kit}"
SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SRC_ROOT="$(cd "$SELF_DIR/.." && pwd)"   # the dwarves-kit repo root when run from its lib/
START="<!-- kit:adopt -->"               # managed-block markers in the consumer CLAUDE.md
END="<!-- /kit:adopt -->"

tmp=""                                   # scratch file; the trap cleans it up on any early exit
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

usage() { echo "usage: adopt.sh [--check | --dry-run | --refresh] [--with <a,b,c>] [--] <target-dir>" >&2; exit 64; }

CHECK=0 DRY=0 REFRESH=0 WITH_ARG=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --check) CHECK=1; shift;;
    --dry-run) DRY=1; shift;;
    --refresh) REFRESH=1; shift;;
    --with) shift; WITH_ARG="${1:-}"; shift;;
    --with=*) WITH_ARG="${1#--with=}"; shift;;
    --) shift; break;;
    -*) usage;;
    *) break;;
  esac
done
TARGET="${1:-}"; [ -n "$TARGET" ] || usage
[ -d "$TARGET" ] || { echo "adopt: target dir not found: $TARGET" >&2; exit 1; }

agents="$TARGET/AGENTS.md"
workflow="$TARGET/WORKFLOW.md"
claude="$TARGET/CLAUDE.md"
marker="$TARGET/docs/verification/README.md"
dotkit="$TARGET/.kit.toml"
project_settings="$TARGET/.claude/settings.json"

is_adopted() {
  # -qxF: the marker must be its own full line (matches how awk strips the block). A substring
  # grep would mis-detect a marker quoted inside prose and skip the append path (review #6).
  [ -f "$agents" ] && [ -f "$marker" ] && [ -f "$claude" ] \
    && grep -qxF "$START" "$claude" 2>/dev/null
}

if [ "$CHECK" -eq 1 ]; then
  is_adopted && { echo "adopted: $TARGET"; exit 0; } || { echo "not adopted: $TARGET"; exit 1; }
fi

git -C "$TARGET" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || echo "adopt: warning: $TARGET is not a git repo (adopting at filesystem level anyway)" >&2

# Resolve a source AGENTS.md: the kit repo (dev) first, then the install.
src_agents=""
for c in "$SRC_ROOT/AGENTS.md" "$KIT_ROOT/AGENTS.md"; do
  [ -f "$c" ] && { src_agents="$c"; break; }
done
[ -n "$src_agents" ] || { echo "adopt: no source AGENTS.md (looked in $SRC_ROOT, $KIT_ROOT)" >&2; exit 1; }

workflow_block() {
  cat <<EOF
# WORKFLOW.md (pointer)

This repo is adopted into the dwarves-kit. The canonical lanes and the lane x phase gate matrix
live in the installed kit: \`$KIT_ROOT/WORKFLOW.md\`. Read that for the lanes and the gate at each
phase boundary. The gate machinery (gate-ledger, ship-gate) parses that copy, not this file.
EOF
}

claude_block() {
  printf '%s\n' "$START"
  printf '## Operating layer (dwarves-kit)\n\n'
  printf '@AGENTS.md\n\n'
  printf 'Before touching code, classify the lane: `bash %s/bin/classify lane classify "<task>"`.\n' "$KIT_ROOT"
  printf 'A full-lane change records its gates via `%s/bin/gate ledger` or the ship-gate blocks the push.\n' "$KIT_ROOT"
  printf '%s\n' "$END"
}

did=0
note() { echo "adopt: would $*"; }

# 1. AGENTS.md -- the operate-contract. NEVER overwritten (even on --refresh).
if [ ! -f "$agents" ]; then
  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "create AGENTS.md (from $src_agents)"; else cp "$src_agents" "$agents"; fi
  did=1
fi

# 2. WORKFLOW.md pointer -- create if absent; --refresh overwrites to current. Write atomically
# (tmp + mv) so a kill / full disk mid-write can't leave a half-written pointer (review #3).
if [ ! -f "$workflow" ] || { [ "$REFRESH" -eq 1 ] && ! cmp -s <(workflow_block) "$workflow"; }; then
  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "write WORKFLOW.md pointer"; else
    tmp="$(mktemp)"; workflow_block > "$tmp"; mv "$tmp" "$workflow"
  fi
  did=1
fi

# 3. CLAUDE.md loader (@AGENTS.md import) -- append once; --refresh replaces the managed block.
if [ ! -f "$claude" ] || ! grep -qxF "$START" "$claude" 2>/dev/null; then
  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "append the CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md loader block"; else
    tmp="$(mktemp)"; { [ -f "$claude" ] && cat "$claude"; printf '\n'; claude_block; } > "$tmp"; mv "$tmp" "$claude"
  fi
  did=1
elif [ "$REFRESH" -eq 1 ]; then
  # Refuse to refresh a block with a START but no END: the awk strip would drop everything from
  # START to EOF and mv would install the truncated file (silent data loss; review CRITICAL #1).
  # This is exactly the legacy single-sentinel shape, so the operator migrates it by hand.
  if ! grep -qxF "$END" "$claude" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "adopt: $claude has '$START' but no '$END' line; refusing --refresh (would truncate)." >&2
    echo "adopt: add an '$END' line after the managed block, or delete the block, then re-run." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "refresh the CLAUDE.md loader block"; did=1; else
    tmp="$(mktemp)"
    # END{if(drop)exit 3}: belt-and-suspenders against an unterminated block slipping past the
    # guard above; the `|| exit` stops us from mv-ing a truncated file when awk bails.
    awk -v s="$START" -v e="$END" '
      $0==s{drop=1; next} drop&&$0==e{drop=0; next} !drop{print}
      END{if(drop) exit 3}' "$claude" > "$tmp" \
      || { echo "adopt: failed to strip the managed block from $claude (unterminated?)" >&2; exit 1; }
    claude_block >> "$tmp"
    if cmp -s "$tmp" "$claude"; then rm -f "$tmp"; else mv "$tmp" "$claude"; did=1; fi
  fi
fi

# 4. proof marker -- presence opts this repo into the ship-gate. NEVER overwritten.
if [ ! -f "$marker" ]; then
  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then note "create docs/verification/README.md (proof marker)"; else
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$marker")"
    cat > "$marker" <<EOF
# Verification (proof-of-done marker)

Presence of this file opts this repo into the dwarves-kit proof-of-done ship-gate. A
behavioral/stateful change owes a recorded run here; the shape per loop type comes from the
install: \`bash $KIT_ROOT/lib/gate/proof-gate.sh contract "<task>"\`.
EOF
  fi
  did=1
fi

# --- SPEC-192 (goal 06): close the per-project override loop -----------------------------

# Resolve the kit-root kit.toml (dev checkout first, then the install) -- same lookup shape
# as src_agents above.
kit_root_toml=""
for c in "$SRC_ROOT/kit.toml" "$KIT_ROOT/kit.toml"; do
  [ -f "$c" ] && { kit_root_toml="$c"; break; }
done

# module -> its hook script basenames (space-separated; empty = hookless -- queue, stats,
# quiz_gate, weekend_batch, bridge are commands/skills with no hook to gate). Kept in sync
# with install.sh's kit_module_hooks() (same doc note there): only board/session/advisor/
# cosmetic carry a hook, so only those need a settings.json entry.
kit_module_hooks() {
  case "$1" in
    board) echo "backlog-stage.sh" ;;
    session) echo "context-readiness.sh output-offload.sh pre-compact-backup.sh post-compact-reinject.sh session-state-save.sh harvest.sh citation-guard.sh" ;;
    advisor) echo "context-hints.sh" ;;
    cosmetic) echo "auto-format.sh notification.sh slop-cleaner.sh statusline.sh codebase-index.sh permission-auto-approve.sh" ;;
    *) echo "" ;;
  esac
}

KIT_KNOWN_MODULES="board session advisor cosmetic queue stats quiz_gate weekend_batch bridge"

# Load the config resolver in a function scope so its own `${1:-}` selftest check (see
# lib/config/kit-config.sh) never sees adopt.sh's own positional parameters (TARGET etc).
_kit_load_config_resolver() {
  # shellcheck source=lib/config/kit-config.sh
  source "$SELF_DIR/config/kit-config.sh"
}
RESOLVER_OK=1
_kit_load_config_resolver 2>/dev/null || RESOLVER_OK=0

# 5. Per-project .kit.toml -- an OPT-IN starter (SPEC-192). Created only if absent; a
# project's own config is NEVER overwritten by adopt, fresh or --refresh (same invariant as
# AGENTS.md / the proof marker). --with (first run only) seeds the named modules `true`;
# every other key seeds the kit-root default it would inherit anyway -- writing the line
# explicitly just makes the override point visible and editable.
if [ -n "$kit_root_toml" ] && [ "$RESOLVER_OK" -eq 1 ]; then
  if [ ! -f "$dotkit" ]; then
    if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then
      note "seed a starter .kit.toml (modules: ${WITH_ARG:-kit-root defaults})"
    else
      with_norm=""
      [ -n "$WITH_ARG" ] && with_norm=" $(echo "$WITH_ARG" | tr ',' ' ' | xargs) "
      tmp="$(mktemp)"
      {
        echo "# .kit.toml -- this PROJECT's override of the kit-root defaults (SPEC-192)."
        echo "# Only the keys you set here matter; every key you omit inherits the kit-root"
        echo "# default at $KIT_ROOT/kit.toml (lib/config/kit-config.sh: project keys WIN)."
        echo "# Re-run \`bash $KIT_ROOT/lib/adopt.sh --refresh <this repo>\` (or /kit:adopt) after"
        echo "# editing [modules] to re-wire this project's .claude/settings.json to match --"
        echo "# adopt reads this file at adopt time; no hook reads it at hook-fire time."
        echo ""
        echo "[modules]"
        for m in $KIT_KNOWN_MODULES; do
          if [ -n "$with_norm" ]; then
            case "$with_norm" in *" $m "*) v=true ;; *) v=false ;; esac
          else
            KIT_CONFIG_ROOT="$(dirname "$kit_root_toml")" KIT_PROJECT_ROOT="$TARGET" \
              v="$(kit_config_get "modules.$m" "false")"
          fi
          echo "$m = $v"
        done
      } > "$tmp"
      mv "$tmp" "$dotkit"
    fi
    did=1
  elif [ -n "$WITH_ARG" ]; then
    echo "adopt: note: $dotkit already exists; --with ignored (edit the file's [modules] section directly)" >&2
  fi
fi

# 6. Per-project hook-module wiring into <target>/.claude/settings.json (SPEC-192). Runs on
# EVERY adopt invocation (fresh or --refresh), reading this project's CURRENT .kit.toml (project
# override, else the kit-root default -- the resolver from goal 01), so a hand-edited .kit.toml
# is picked up the next time adopt runs. Never on hook-fire (Not: runtime per-call module
# toggling). A jq MERGE, never a settings.json rewrite: only kit-module hook entries
# (dwarves-kit/hooks/*) are added/removed; every other entry in the file is preserved untouched.
# Command/skill modules (queue, stats, quiz_gate, weekend_batch, bridge) have no hook, so they
# never touch settings.json regardless of their .kit.toml value.
if [ -n "$kit_root_toml" ] && [ "$RESOLVER_OK" -eq 1 ] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  settings_src=""
  for c in "$SRC_ROOT/settings.json" "$KIT_ROOT/settings.json"; do
    [ -f "$c" ] && { settings_src="$c"; break; }
  done
  if [ -n "$settings_src" ]; then
    HOOKED_MODULES="board session advisor cosmetic"
    enabled_list="" wired_hook_names=""
    for m in $HOOKED_MODULES; do
      KIT_CONFIG_ROOT="$(dirname "$kit_root_toml")" KIT_PROJECT_ROOT="$TARGET" \
        v="$(kit_config_get "modules.$m" "false")"
      if [ "$v" = "true" ]; then
        enabled_list="$enabled_list $m"
        wired_hook_names="$wired_hook_names $(kit_module_hooks "$m")"
      fi
    done
    wired_hook_names="$(echo "$wired_hook_names" | xargs)"

    hook_re=""
    for h in $wired_hook_names; do
      esc="$(printf '%s' "$h" | sed 's/\./\\./g')"
      if [ -z "$hook_re" ]; then hook_re="$esc"; else hook_re="$hook_re|$esc"; fi
    done

    if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then
      note "wire $project_settings for modules:${enabled_list:-<none>} (hooks:${wired_hook_names:-none})"
    else
      before_wired=""
      [ -f "$project_settings" ] && before_wired="$(jq -r '[.hooks // {} | to_entries[]? | .value[]? | .hooks[]? | .command] | .[]' "$project_settings" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'dwarves-kit/hooks/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.sh' | sort -u)"

      filtered="$(mktemp)"
      if [ -n "$hook_re" ]; then
        jq --arg re "$hook_re" '
          .hooks |= (
            to_entries | map(
              .value |= (
                map(.hooks |= map(select(.command | test($re)))) | map(select(.hooks | length > 0))
              )
            ) | from_entries
          )
        ' "$settings_src" > "$filtered" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"hooks":{}}' > "$filtered"
      else
        echo '{"hooks":{}}' > "$filtered"
      fi

      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$project_settings")"
      # One code path for both "no project settings.json yet" and "re-wiring an existing
      # one" (a missing file reads as {}): strip any prior kit-module hook (dwarves-kit/
      # hooks/*, added by an earlier adopt run), then union in the currently-enabled set.
      # Canonicalized (jq -S, arrays sorted by their own JSON text) so a re-run over an
      # UNCHANGED .kit.toml reproduces byte-identical output -- adopt's own idempotency
      # invariant (test-adopt.sh), not just "the same hook names, any order".
      existing_json='{}'
      [ -f "$project_settings" ] && existing_json="$(cat "$project_settings")"
      merged="$(jq -n --argjson existing "$existing_json" --slurpfile kit "$filtered" '
        $existing as $ex | ($kit[0].hooks // {}) as $kh
        | $ex
        | .hooks = (
            ((($ex.hooks // {}) | to_entries
              | map(.value |= (
                  map(.hooks |= map(select(.command | tostring | contains("dwarves-kit/hooks/") | not)))
                  | map(select(.hooks | length > 0))
                ))
             ) + ($kh | to_entries))
            | group_by(.key)
            | map({
                key: .[0].key,
                value: ([.[].value[]] | unique_by(tostring) | sort_by(tostring))
              })
            | sort_by(.key)
            | from_entries
          )
      ' 2>/dev/null)"
      if [ -n "$merged" ] && echo "$merged" | jq -S '.' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "$merged" | jq -S '.' > "$project_settings"
      else
        echo "adopt: warning: jq merge of $project_settings failed; left untouched" >&2
      fi
      rm -f "$filtered"

      after_wired=""
      [ -f "$project_settings" ] && after_wired="$(jq -r '[.hooks // {} | to_entries[]? | .value[]? | .hooks[]? | .command] | .[]' "$project_settings" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'dwarves-kit/hooks/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.sh' | sort -u)"
      [ "$before_wired" != "$after_wired" ] && did=1
      echo "adopt: project hook-module wiring for $TARGET -> modules:${enabled_list:-<none>}"
    fi
  fi
fi

if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "adopt: --dry-run for $TARGET ($([ "$did" -eq 1 ] && echo 'changes above' || echo 'already adopted, nothing to do'))"
else
  echo "adopt: $TARGET ($([ "$did" -eq 1 ] && echo updated || echo 'already adopted, no-op'))"
fi

1	# AGENTS.md: the operating layer
2	
3	> Tool-agnostic front door. Any agent runtime (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, a
4	> human) reads this first to learn how work is done in this repo. It carries the
5	> portable operate-contract: what to read, how to run a unit of work, when work
6	> is done, and when to stop and ask.
7	
8	## Enforcement boundary (read this first)
9	
10	**This file is a contract, not a guardrail.** Enforcement is Claude-Code-only: the
11	hooks (safety-gate, push-to-main blocker, anti-rationalization Stop hook, the
12	verification pipeline) are what actually block bad outcomes, and they run only
13	under Claude Code. Under any other runtime (Codex, Gemini, a bare LLM)
14	`AGENTS.md` is **advisory only**: it tells an agent what to do, but nothing
15	enforces it. Do not assume the guardrails are portable. They are not, until the
16	v3.x multi-runtime agent-hook work lands. See `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md` (honesty rule:
17	never over-claim portable enforcement) and `CLAUDE.md` for the CC-specific layer
18	(hooks, slash commands, plugin). The full layering contract, which hook
19	backstops what and why (hard / advisory / convenience), is
20	`docs/architecture.md` "Hook fallback layer".
21	
22	The rest of this file is four portable zones. The goal-crafter
23	(`commands/assign.md`) projects them into a six-section `/goal` (see "How a goal
24	is composed" at the end).
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 1. Read in this order
29	
30	Orient before you touch anything. Read top to bottom; stop when you have enough.
31	
32	1. **AGENTS.md** (this file) - how work is done here; the operate-contract.
33	2. **CLAUDE.md** - the Claude-Code layer: stack, structure, rules, hooks, commands, plugin.
34	3. **docs/specs/SPEC-NNN-<slug>.md** - the active spec; the shared contract for the cycle. Read its `## Verification` and `## After state` before implementing.
35	4. **docs/architecture.md** / **WORKFLOW.md** / **docs/data-flow.md** - reference, not required per task. Read `docs/architecture.md` for how the pieces fit; `docs/data-flow.md` for how DATA moves (the signal path telemetry -> proposal -> board, the ledger write/read paths, the module map); read `WORKFLOW.md` for the lanes and the gate at each phase boundary, and its "Mega-goal delegate execution" section for how a multi-sub-goal mega-goal run dispatches (delegate mode: one fresh headless session per sub-goal; `/goal` stays the official outer loop either way).
36	
37	## 2. Task loop
38	
39	How to do one unit of work. The smallest verifiable increment, verified, committed.
40	
41	0. **Take work.** Handed a task: use it. **Handed a WAVE (2+ items approved in one
42	   conversation): enqueue every item as a board row FIRST (queued; the in-flight one
43	   executing), then pull them one at a time.** Work that never touches the board is
44	   invisible to the board's state machine even when its runs are ledgered, the gap an
45	   operator caught live on 2026-06-10 (SPEC-064). Not handed one: pull the board's top queued item,
46	   `bash lib/board/backlog.sh next`, claim it (goal-registry) and flip it to `claimed` (the
47	   `/kit:assign --next` flow). The BACKLOG is the board; its Status column is the state
48	   machine (`queued -> claimed -> speccing -> validated -> executing -> shipped`, + parked/
49	   dropped). Operator-named work is unchanged; pull is an additional trigger, never a daemon.
50	1. **Classify the type, then size the lane.** `bash lib/classify/task-type-classify.sh classify "<task>"`
51	   first: `spec-feature` picks a lane below; any other type (incident / reconcile / operate /
52	   planning / learning / eval / research / review / doc / migration / data-tool) runs its TYPE LOOP per
53	   `WORKFLOW.md ## Type loops`, with its executor from the registry's `agent` column. The lane
54	   is STILL sized for every type (it is the evidence contract ship-gate enforces via the spec's
55	   `Lane:` header; the type is the content contract , `WORKFLOW.md ### Lane x type composition`). For code:
56	   pick `tiny` / `normal` / `full` / `bug` / `backfill` per `WORKFLOW.md`; when in doubt between
57	   two lanes, take the heavier one. **Between classification and done comes the grill** (`/kit:grill`, or its
58	   one-question-at-a-time discipline driven inline): interview until the task is actually
59	   understood, type-shaped questions, recommended answers, contradictions checked against the
60	   repo, answers WRITTEN as they resolve (glossary / sparse ADR / the goal draft's Context).
61	   Tiny lane exempt. **Record the grill's disposition either way** (SPEC-063):
62	   `bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh record <rid> grill ran "<N> branches resolved"`, or, when the
63	   conversation already resolved the banks, `... record <rid> grill skipped "<why>"`; a
64	   skip without a reason is invisible to telemetry, which defeats the point.
65	   **Then phase 0: define the done scenario**
66	   (`bash lib/gate/proof-gate.sh contract "<task>"` + the type's test-design dialect,
67	   test-design-standard §5b) BEFORE any work runs; the grill's answers are the done's raw
68	   material, and the goal draft carries the `Done =` line.
69	2. **Read the spec and its acceptance criteria.** For a spec-driven task: the active spec's task row, its AC, its `## Verification`, and its `## After state`. No spec (tiny lane): the one obvious edit.
70	3. **Implement the smallest verifiable increment.** One logical change. No speculative features, no premature abstraction; clarity over cleverness.
71	4. **Verify.** Run the spec's `## Verification` command (or the lane's check). Do not claim a result you did not run.
72	5. **Commit.** Conventional commit, one logical change. No spec/ticket IDs in the subject line.
73	
74	If you cannot make progress, see zone 4 (Pause if) and stop with a named blocker note. Do not churn.
75	
76	**One rid per run, derived from the branch (SPEC-070).** `<rid>` everywhere below is `$(bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh rid)`: the branch slug (`type/` prefix stripped), the same key `hooks/ship-gate.sh` checks at push, so assign-time records and ship-time enforcement meet with no mirror re-records. Derive it AFTER the work branch exists; the verb refuses master/main/detached.
77	
78	**Show the road, then your position on it (SPEC-063).** Right after a lane is committed,
79	print the checklist the run will walk: `bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh plan <lane>`. At each phase
80	entry, print where the run stands: `bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh progress <rid> <lane>`
81	(one status line: `<rid> · <lane> · step k/n (<phase>)` + the ✓/▶/· checklist). For the
82	full story of a past or in-flight run: `bash lib/telemetry/lane-telemetry.sh trace <rid>`.
83	
84	**Escalate the review for enforcement surfaces (SPEC-069).** A run touching `lib/` or
85	`hooks/` uses `/kit:review-team` (multi-lens), not a single reviewer.
86	
87	**Record your gates (ADR-0024).** When you run a phase gate (`/kit:spec`, `/kit:spec-validate`, `/kit:execute`, `/kit:review`, `/kit:docs`, `/kit:ship`, ...), record it so the run is auditable: `bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh record <rid> <Phase> ran`; record a deliberate skip as `skipped "<why>"`. The `ship-gate` hook refuses a push whose lane has a required gate with no `ran`/`override` entry. Phase ORDER matters too: the lane plan is the V-model descent order; `bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh descent <rid> <lane>` names out-of-order records, surfaced at ship as an advisory (SPEC-076). Full convention + the logged-override path: WORKFLOW.md "## Gate ledger and ship enforcement".
88	
89	**Gates are also MEASURED, not just recorded (SPEC-129).** Beside `ran`/`skipped`, `bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh outcome <rid> <phase> start|end [caught=<bool>]` brackets a gate with a duration and whether it caught a defect, on the same additive marker convention (a fourth `| OUTCOME |` line beside `| GATE | / | DEBT | / | TOKENS |`; existing readers ignore it). The only live emitter today is `hooks/ship-gate.sh` at the ship boundary, HOOK-ENFORCED but ship-boundary-only, not yet per-phase; read it back with `outcome-read`. **A parallel wave closes the SPEC-number race at dispatch, not at spec-time (SPEC-128).** `lib/queue/orchestrate.sh`'s own wavefront dispatch atomically reserves a number per sub-goal via `bash lib/spec/spec-next.sh reserve` (a portable mkdir-mutex over an append-only reservations ledger) before any worker can race `spec-next.sh next`; a standalone session still calls `spec-next.sh next` directly, unaffected. **Generate the confirmation table, never hand-author it (SPEC-132).** `bash lib/gate/proof-table-gen.sh <rid>` renders `docs/verification/generated/<rid>.md` from the same gate/run ledger (surfacing the OUTCOME column above when present); see `docs/verification/README.md` "Generators write run ledgers, never the canonical." Full detail on all three, plus the two advisory measurement gates (coverage-delta, mutation-smoke): WORKFLOW.md "## Gate ledger and ship enforcement" and "## Advisory measurement gates".
90	
91	## 3. Done means
92	
93	A task or goal is done only when **its acceptance criteria are met AND the
94	verifier actually ran the check**, not when you claim they pass. Self-reported
95	"done" is not proof. The check compares against the `Done =` scenario defined at
96	phase 0, whatever the work's type (PHILOSOPHY §6 N3): if no done scenario was
97	defined before the work ran, the work was not assignable, and "done" has nothing
98	to be measured against.
99	
100	Concretely, done means: **acceptance criteria met, the check actually ran (not
101	just asserted), review recorded + report written, and the final response says
102	what changed and what was not attempted.** If you could not run the check, report
103	that plainly; the anti-rationalization hook is the backstop for premature
104	completion under Claude Code, but the honesty obligation is yours under any
105	runtime.
106	
107	**Deployable-done (ADR-0028, reusing ADR-0025).** DEPLOYABLE work is anything that runs
108	somewhere , a service, a daemon, a feature behind a flag, or any change `lib/gate/proof-ledger.sh
109	classify` puts in its `stateful` class (deploy / rollout / production / migration / schema /
110	database / persistent-state signals in the diff or commit subjects). For deployable work,
111	`done` = **a deploy-proof + a UAT/acceptance run**: the existing ADR-0025 stateful proof
112	shape (a recorded run with `Command:`/`Exit:` AND a `rollback` note or `[UNAVAILABLE:
113	reason]`) PLUS a UAT/acceptance line recording that the change was exercised in the target
114	environment and accepted. This is enforced at ship by the SAME `hooks/ship-gate.sh` ->
115	`proof-ledger.sh check` wall every stateful change already passes through , the ship-gate
116	already DETECTS deployability (it classifies `stateful`), so a deployable item marked done
117	without the deploy-proof is blocked exactly like any other unproven stateful change, or
118	needs a logged override (`proof-ledger.sh override <slug> "<reason>"`). INERT, library,
119	refactor, and docs work (the `inert`/`behavioral` classes) is unchanged , it owes no
120	deploy-proof or UAT.
121	
122	**Understanding is a separate, advisory axis (ADR-0031) -- orthogonal to Done means above.**
123	A design record (before build) and an explainer + quiz nudge (at merge) gate the human's
124	PARTICIPATION and ATTENTION, never correctness: they never change what "done" means here, never
125	block a correct build, and are not enforced by any hook the way the verification gates are.
126	Full model: `WORKFLOW.md` "## The understanding axis".
127	
128	## 4. Pause if (ask a human)
129	
130	Stop and ask a human before acting on any of these. These are decisions with
131	direction or irreversible cost that a goal loop must not make on its own.
132	
133	- **Architecture direction** - a change to how the pieces fit, a new component, an interface or data-model shape.
134	- **Source-of-truth hierarchy** - which file or section is canonical when two disagree (for example, moving the operate-contract between `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `WORKFLOW.md`).
135	- **Validation removal** - weakening, deleting, or bypassing a test, an assertion, a hook, or any guardrail.
136	- **Risk-classification change** - moving work to a lighter lane, or narrowing a `full`-lane trigger (auth, authz, hooks, data model, data loss, audit/security, external provider, API contract, migration).
137	- **Privacy / security** - secrets, credentials, access scope, anything that touches what data leaves the repo or who can reach it.
138	
139	When you pause: write the named blocker, state the decision you are not making and why, and stop.
140	
141	## Self-intro (what is running and why)
142	
143	Every `/kit:` command opens its FIRST reply with a one-line banner, `[kit:<name>] <one-line purpose>`, the purpose derived from that command's own frontmatter `description`. Every dispatched agent opens its report the same way (`[kit:<agent>] <one-line purpose>`). One banner line, then the real output; never repeated mid-run, and a mode whose contract is stricter (e.g. `/kit:start --brief`'s single line) wins over the banner. A new user should never have to guess what is running or why it fired. Wired concretely into the highest-traffic entries (`commands/start.md`, `commands/assign.md`, `commands/execute.md`); every other command adopts on next touch, and this contract covers them meanwhile.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## How the kit composes (subsystem modules)
148	
149	The kit is a **toolbox of self-contained subsystem modules under `lib/<subsystem>/`**
150	(board, classify, gate, goal, queue, session, spec, stats, telemetry, plus the ledger
151	substrate and single-purpose orphans), not one appliance you switch on. "tool" vs "lib"
152	describes a module's SURFACE (leaf/human vs internal-helper), not its location; there is no
153	separate `tools/` tree. Each multi-verb subsystem exposes a **standalone `<subsystem> <verb>`
154	command** (`board next`, `gate ledger ...`, `classify ...`, `spec ...`, `goal ...`,
155	`session ...`) that forwards to the script owning that verb; the internal
156	`bash lib/<subsystem>/<file>.sh` form used throughout the task loop still works unchanged.
157	There is no `kit` uber-dispatcher, each command's own `--help` is the discovery surface. The
158	read plane is **`stats`**: a stateless projection recomputed on demand from the append-only
159	ledger, never a persisted second source of truth.
160	
161	Adoption is **layered, not all-or-nothing**. `install.sh` wires the essential spine
162	unconditionally (the spec-driven development (SDD) ship discipline: safety-gate, ship-gate, spec-drift-guard,
163	secrets-guard, commit-format, anti-rationalization) and opt-in modules only when asked
164	(`install.sh --with board,session,stats,...`), recording the enabled set in the consumer's
165	`kit.toml [modules]` manifest, an install artifact that records the choice, never read at
166	runtime. Full adoption model + rationale: `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md` and `README.md`.
167	
168	---
169	
170	## How a goal is composed (for `commands/assign.md`)
171	
172	The goal-crafter projects these four zones into a six-section `/goal`. The mapping
173	is a **composition, not 1:1**: two of the six sections come from the active spec,
174	not from this file. Keep the four zone names stable; renaming one without updating
175	`commands/assign.md` breaks the projection.
176	
177	| `/goal` section | Source |
178	|---|---|
179	| Context-to-read | AGENTS.md zone 1 (Read in this order) |
180	| Constraints | CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md rules |
181	| Operating rules | AGENTS.md zone 2 (Task loop) |
182	| Validation loop | the active spec's `## Verification` |
183	| Done-when | AGENTS.md zone 3 (Done means) + the active spec's `## After state` |
184	| Pause-if | AGENTS.md zone 4 (Pause if) |
185

**Record your gates (ADR-0024).** When you run a phase gate (`/kit:spec`, `/kit:spec-validate`, `/kit:execute`, `/kit:review`, `/kit:docs`, `/kit:ship`, ...), record it so the run is auditable: `bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh record <rid> <Phase> ran`; record a deliberate skip as `skipped "<why>"`. The `ship-gate` hook refuses a push whose lane has a required gate with no `ran`/`override` entry. Phase ORDER matters too: the lane plan is the V-model descent order; `bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh descent <rid> <lane>` names out-of-order records, surfaced at ship as an advisory (SPEC-076). Full convention + the logged-override path: WORKFLOW.md "## Gate ledger and ship enforcement".

**Gates are also MEASURED, not just recorded (SPEC-129).** Beside `ran`/`skipped`, `bash lib/gate/gate-ledger.sh outcome <rid> <phase> start|end [caught=<bool>]` brackets a gate with a duration and whether it caught a defect, on the same additive marker convention (a fourth `| OUTCOME |` line beside `| GATE | / | DEBT | / | TOKENS |`; existing readers ignore it). The only live emitter today is `hooks/ship-gate.sh` at the ship boundary, HOOK-ENFORCED but ship-boundary-only, not yet per-phase; read it back with `outcome-read`. **A parallel wave closes the SPEC-number race at dispatch, not at spec-time (SPEC-128).** `lib/queue/orchestrate.sh`'s own wavefront dispatch atomically reserves a number per sub-goal via `bash lib/spec/spec-next.sh reserve` (a portable mkdir-mutex over an append-only reservations ledger) before any worker can race `spec-next.sh next`; a standalone session still calls `spec-next.sh next` directly, unaffected. **Generate the confirmation table, never hand-author it (SPEC-132).** `bash lib/gate/proof-table-gen.sh <rid>` renders `docs/verification/generated/<rid>.md` from the same gate/run ledger (surfacing the OUTCOME column above when present); see `docs/verification/README.md` "Generators write run ledgers, never the canonical." Full detail on all three, plus the two advisory measurement gates (coverage-delta, mutation-smoke): WORKFLOW.md "## Gate ledger and ship enforcement" and "## Advisory measurement gates".

## 3. Done means

A task or goal is done only when **its acceptance criteria are met AND the
verifier actually ran the check**, not when you claim they pass. Self-reported
"done" is not proof. The check compares against the `Done =` scenario defined at
phase 0, whatever the work's type (PHILOSOPHY §6 N3): if no done scenario was
defined before the work ran, the work was not assignable, and "done" has nothing
to be measured against.

Concretely, done means: **acceptance criteria met, the check actually ran (not
just asserted), review recorded + report written, and the final response says
what changed and what was not attempted.** If you could not run the check, report
that plainly; the anti-rationalization hook is the backstop for premature
completion under Claude Code, but the honesty obligation is yours under any
runtime.

**Deployable-done (ADR-0028, reusing ADR-0025).** DEPLOYABLE work is anything that runs
somewhere , a service, a daemon, a feature behind a flag, or any change `lib/gate/proof-ledger.sh
classify` puts in its `stateful` class (deploy / rollout / production / migration / schema /
database / persistent-state signals in the diff or commit subjects). For deployable work,
`done` = **a deploy-proof + a UAT/acceptance run**: the existing ADR-0025 stateful proof
shape (a recorded run with `Command:`/`Exit:` AND a `rollback` note or `[UNAVAILABLE:
reason]`) PLUS a UAT/acceptance line recording that the change was exercised in the target
environment and accepted. This is enforced at ship by the SAME `hooks/ship-gate.sh` ->
`proof-ledger.sh check` wall every stateful change already passes through , the ship-gate
already DETECTS deployability (it classifies `stateful`), so a deployable item marked done
without the deploy-proof is blocked exactly like any other unproven stateful change, or
needs a logged override (`proof-ledger.sh override <slug> "<reason>"`). INERT, library,
refactor, and docs work (the `inert`/`behavioral` classes) is unchanged , it owes no
deploy-proof or UAT.

**Understanding is a separate, advisory axis (ADR-0031) -- orthogonal to Done means above.**
A design record (before build) and an explainer + quiz nudge (at merge) gate the human's
PARTICIPATION and ATTENTION, never correctness: they never change what "done" means here, never
block a correct build, and are not enforced by any hook the way the verification gates are.
Full model: `WORKFLOW.md` "## The understanding axis".

## 4. Pause if (ask a human)

Stop and ask a human before acting on any of these. These are decisions with
direction or irreversible cost that a goal loop must not make on its own.

- **Architecture direction** - a change to how the pieces fit, a new component, an interface or data-model shape.
- **Source-of-truth hierarchy** - which file or section is canonical when two disagree (for example, moving the operate-contract between `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `WORKFLOW.md`).
- **Validation removal** - weakening, deleting, or bypassing a test, an assertion, a hook, or any guardrail.
- **Risk-classification change** - moving work to a lighter lane, or narrowing a `full`-lane trigger (auth, authz, hooks, data model, data loss, audit/security, external provider, API contract, migration).
- **Privacy / security** - secrets, credentials, access scope, anything that touches what data leaves the repo or who can reach it.

When you pause: write the named blocker, state the decision you are not making and why, and stop.

## Self-intro (what is running and why)

Every `/kit:` command opens its FIRST reply with a one-line banner, `[kit:<name>] <one-line purpose>`, the purpose derived from that command's own frontmatter `description`. Every dispatched agent opens its report the same way (`[kit:<agent>] <one-line purpose>`). One banner line, then the real output; never repeated mid-run, and a mode whose contract is stricter (e.g. `/kit:start --brief`'s single line) wins over the banner. A new user should never have to guess what is running or why it fired. Wired concretely into the highest-traffic entries (`commands/start.md`, `commands/assign.md`, `commands/execute.md`); every other command adopts on next touch, and this contract covers them meanwhile.

---

## How the kit composes (subsystem modules)

The kit is a **toolbox of self-contained subsystem modules under `lib/<subsystem>/`**
(board, classify, gate, goal, queue, session, spec, stats, telemetry, plus the ledger
substrate and single-purpose orphans), not one appliance you switch on. "tool" vs "lib"
describes a module's SURFACE (leaf/human vs internal-helper), not its location; there is no
separate `tools/` tree. Each multi-verb subsystem exposes a **standalone `<subsystem> <verb>`
command** (`board next`, `gate ledger ...`, `classify ...`, `spec ...`, `goal ...`,
`session ...`) that forwards to the script owning that verb; the internal
`bash lib/<subsystem>/<file>.sh` form used throughout the task loop still works unchanged.
There is no `kit` uber-dispatcher, each command's own `--help` is the discovery surface. The
read plane is **`stats`**: a stateless projection recomputed on demand from the append-only
ledger, never a persisted second source of truth.

Adoption is **layered, not all-or-nothing**. `install.sh` wires the essential spine
unconditionally (the spec-driven development (SDD) ship discipline: safety-gate, ship-gate, spec-drift-guard,
secrets-guard, commit-format, anti-rationalization) and opt-in modules only when asked
(`install.sh --with board,session,stats,...`), recording the enabled set in the consumer's
`kit.toml [modules]` manifest, an install artifact that records the choice, never read at
runtime. Full adoption model + rationale: `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md` and `README.md`.

---

## How a goal is composed (for `commands/assign.md`)

The goal-crafter projects these four zones into a six-section `/goal`. The mapping
is a **composition, not 1:1**: two of the six sections come from the active spec,
not from this file. Keep the four zone names stable; renaming one without updating
`commands/assign.md` breaks the projection.

| `/goal` section | Source |
|---|---|
| Context-to-read | AGENTS.md zone 1 (Read in this order) |
| Constraints | CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md rules |
| Operating rules | AGENTS.md zone 2 (Task loop) |
| Validation loop | the active spec's `## Verification` |
| Done-when | AGENTS.md zone 3 (Done means) + the active spec's `## After state` |
| Pause-if | AGENTS.md zone 4 (Pause if) |

51	## Size the work first (risk-tiered intake)
52	Pick a lane before you start. Smaller work skips ceremony.
53	
54	| Lane   | When | Path |
55	|--------|------|------|
56	| tiny   | typo, copy, comment, one obvious edit | edit, verify, done. No spec. |
57	| normal | one bounded feature or fix | /spec, /execute, /review, /ship |
58	| full   | touches auth, authz, hooks, data model, data loss, audit/security, an external provider, an API contract, a migration, or weakens validation | /think, /spec, /spec-validate, /execute, /review-team, /docs, /ship, /retro |
59	| bug    | a defect, regression, or failing test (not a new feature) | /debug (root cause before any fix), then /review |
60	| backfill | brownfield: review an existing codebase and write the operating-layer docs (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / specs) | review the code, write the docs. Doc-output only; no app-behavior change, no app-code edits. /spec optional. |
61	
62	When in doubt between two lanes, take the heavier one. Anything in the full-lane
63	trigger list uses the full lane unless you explicitly narrow the scope and say why.

66	check`): once a lane is chosen, it re-classifies the task text and warns + logs (to
67	`completeness.log`, reviewed at `/kit:ship`) when the choice is lighter than the
68	deterministic floor, so an under-sized `full`/`bug` task does not slip through silently.

71	## Type loops (the non-code cycles)
72	
73	Lanes size the EVIDENCE contract for ALL work (see the composition rule below); the loop content is the type's. The classifier's other eleven types each get their own right-sized cycle
74	(PHILOSOPHY §6 N1). Same intake either way: `lib/classify/task-type-classify.sh` names the type; code work
75	picks a lane above, everything else runs its type's loop below. Chat stays chat, a loop engages
76	when a task is being executed, not on every message. The executor per type (preassigned or
77	dynamic) lives in the registry (`docs/verification/task-types.md`, `agent` column); the proof
78	artifact and rigor live there too.
79	
80	**Phase 0 is universal (PHILOSOPHY §6 N3): every loop starts with the grill, then the done
81	scenario.** First `/kit:grill`, the type-shaped intake interview (one question at a time,
82	recommended answers, write-as-you-go; tiny exempt). Then define the done scenario,
83	the proof contract (`bash lib/gate/proof-gate.sh contract "<task>"`) plus the test design in the
84	type's dialect (test-design-standard §5b), BEFORE any phase below runs. What follows is what
85	gets compared against that definition when the work claims done (the V-model right arm,
86	type-agnostic).
87	
88	| Type | Loop (entry -> phases -> exit) |
89	|------|-------------------------------|
90	| research | frame the question -> multi-modal sweep (parallel angles) -> adversarially verify every load-bearing claim -> cited report |
91	| review | scope the artifact (diff/PR/branch) -> pick lens count (single, or multi per the escalation rule) -> dispatch read-only reviewer(s) -> merge + Route findings (SPEC-078) -> verdict -> record (spec `## Review` or report) |
92	| eval | frame + define metrics -> hand-verify seed data -> climb the test ladder (smoke -> live) -> TEST-REPORT with falsifiability controls -> verdict |
93	| doc | two entry paths (SPEC-073/ID-060): code-diff-triggered, diff sweep (what changed) -> update every affected doc; OR standalone revision, content brief (what the doc must say + for whom) -> rewrite. Both exit through doc-verifier confirming docs match code |
94	| migration | inventory the estate -> dry-run on a copy -> staged apply -> verify + record the run -> rollback path proven |
95	| data-tool | spec/port the surface -> build -> recorded live run + negative control -> Done gate (proof-of-done indexes the run ledgers) |
96	| incident | alert/symptom -> triage (witr/logs) -> root-cause BEFORE any fix (/kit:debug discipline) -> fix/mitigate -> INC-NNN record -> monitoring follow-up |
97	| reconcile | inventory the estate -> classify conform/drift -> migrate/fix -> reference-fix -> gate check |
98	| operate | trigger (schedule/operator) -> pre-checks -> run the procedure -> record the run -> alert on deviation |
99	| planning | gather state (board + PRs + calendar) -> prioritize -> enqueue/re-rank board rows -> digest |
100	| learning | ingest material -> explain/companion -> practice -> self-check >= the track's bar |
101	| spec-feature | (code) pick a lane in "Size the work first" above |
102	
103	### Lane x type composition (SPEC-074 / ID-066)
104	
105	The classifiers always emit BOTH a lane and a type; every (lane, type) pair is legal.
106	Two axes, two contracts:
107	
108	- **The type names the CONTENT contract**: which loop steps run, which proof dialect
109	  is owed, which executor (registry: `docs/verification/task-types.md`).
110	- **The lane names the EVIDENCE contract**: which canonical phases are measure-twice
111	  (the depth matrix above). The ship-gate enforces the spec's `Lane:` header
112	  regardless of type; the lane is what blocks a push, the type is what shapes the work.
113	
114	Mapping rule (the lived wave-1 practice, now written): loop steps execute INSIDE the
115	canonical phases (a loop's "sweep"/"dry-run"/"triage" is its build; its "frame the
116	question" is think/spec). A matrix-required phase with no equivalent loop step is
117	recorded `skipped "<loop-step note>"`, which disposes it (SPEC-063), never silently.
118	
119	Three precedence facts, already true in code, pinned in the suites:
120	
121	1. **Proof class**: tiny/backfill lane short-circuits to `inert` BEFORE stateful
122	   keywords and the registry type default (full order: lane-inert > stateful keywords > registry default > behavioral; SPEC-071 added the registry step), so `fix a typo in the
123	   incident runbook` (tiny + incident) owes no INC record.
124	2. **bug + incident** (`fix the prod crash, alert firing`): the incident loop's
125	   root-cause-before-fix IS the bug lane's debug discipline; incident supplies the
126	   loop content + INC-NNN artifact, bug supplies the bug-lane plan (6 phases, 3 required gates: build, review, debug).
127	3. **Degenerate lanes**: tiny (2 phases: build + review since SPEC-076) and backfill (5 phases) bound the ceremony
128	   for ANY type; a heavy type on a tiny diff stays tiny (see fact 1).
129	
130	A loop is right-sized or it is wrong: a research loop that feels like ceremony for a research
131	task is a defect, not rigor. Tool comparisons are evals; test-design passes ride the owning
132	work item's test-plan phase; cleanup/drift sweeps are the reconcile loop; deployments ride
133	migration (same dry-run + rollback shape); agent-org config rides spec-feature lanes.

136	| Phase    | Command | Exit when | Enforced by |
137	|----------|---------|-----------|-------------|

142	| UI design (opt-in, downstream) | /kit:ui-design | brief -> generate (frontend-design) -> critique -> revise | advisory (downstream only) |
143	| Spec     | /kit:spec | spec exists, Status: DRAFT | spec-drift-guard hook |

146	| Build    | /kit:execute or /kit:next | tasks checked, verifier PASS | verification pipeline (worker, verifier, fix; max 2) |
147	| Review   | /kit:review or /kit:review-team | review verdict recorded | advisory |

162	> 10-second view; this section + the SVG are the full V.)

164	The cycle table above is the canonical phase list. This section reads it as a **V**.
165	The **left arm BUILDS**: each phase produces an artifact and statically reviews it
166	(verification, "did we build this right?"). The **right arm TESTS**: it executes the
167	test that validates each artifact and reports (validation, "does it actually work?").
168	**Build** is the vertex. The V-model's core move is that every artifact gets *two*
169	checks: a static review when it is produced (left/vertex) and a dynamic test later
170	(right). The kit does not shift test design up the left arm (it has one late
171	`/kit:test-plan` step), so the test-design + execution wing sits on the right.

173	```

| migration | inventory the estate -> dry-run on a copy -> staged apply -> verify + record the run -> rollback path proven |
| data-tool | spec/port the surface -> build -> recorded live run + negative control -> Done gate (proof-of-done indexes the run ledgers) |
| incident | alert/symptom -> triage (witr/logs) -> root-cause BEFORE any fix (/kit:debug discipline) -> fix/mitigate -> INC-NNN record -> monitoring follow-up |
| reconcile | inventory the estate -> classify conform/drift -> migrate/fix -> reference-fix -> gate check |
| operate | trigger (schedule/operator) -> pre-checks -> run the procedure -> record the run -> alert on deviation |
| planning | gather state (board + PRs + calendar) -> prioritize -> enqueue/re-rank board rows -> digest |
| learning | ingest material -> explain/companion -> practice -> self-check >= the track's bar |
| spec-feature | (code) pick a lane in "Size the work first" above |

### Lane x type composition (SPEC-074 / ID-066)

The classifiers always emit BOTH a lane and a type; every (lane, type) pair is legal.
Two axes, two contracts:

- **The type names the CONTENT contract**: which loop steps run, which proof dialect
  is owed, which executor (registry: `docs/verification/task-types.md`).
- **The lane names the EVIDENCE contract**: which canonical phases are measure-twice
  (the depth matrix above). The ship-gate enforces the spec's `Lane:` header
  regardless of type; the lane is what blocks a push, the type is what shapes the work.

Mapping rule (the lived wave-1 practice, now written): loop steps execute INSIDE the
canonical phases (a loop's "sweep"/"dry-run"/"triage" is its build; its "frame the
question" is think/spec). A matrix-required phase with no equivalent loop step is
recorded `skipped "<loop-step note>"`, which disposes it (SPEC-063), never silently.

Three precedence facts, already true in code, pinned in the suites:

1. **Proof class**: tiny/backfill lane short-circuits to `inert` BEFORE stateful
   keywords and the registry type default (full order: lane-inert > stateful keywords > registry default > behavioral; SPEC-071 added the registry step), so `fix a typo in the
   incident runbook` (tiny + incident) owes no INC record.
2. **bug + incident** (`fix the prod crash, alert firing`): the incident loop's
   root-cause-before-fix IS the bug lane's debug discipline; incident supplies the
   loop content + INC-NNN artifact, bug supplies the bug-lane plan (6 phases, 3 required gates: build, review, debug).
3. **Degenerate lanes**: tiny (2 phases: build + review since SPEC-076) and backfill (5 phases) bound the ceremony
   for ANY type; a heavy type on a tiny diff stays tiny (see fact 1).

A loop is right-sized or it is wrong: a research loop that feels like ceremony for a research
task is a defect, not rigor. Tool comparisons are evals; test-design passes ride the owning
work item's test-plan phase; cleanup/drift sweeps are the reconcile loop; deployments ride
migration (same dry-run + rollback shape); agent-org config rides spec-feature lanes.

## The cycle (phase, exit, enforcer)
| Phase    | Command | Exit when | Enforced by |
|----------|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Think    | /kit:think | decision brief written (if BUILD) | advisory |
| Design (opt-in) | /kit:design | solution agreed + appended to the brief | advisory |
| Design critique (opt-in) | /kit:devs-team, /kit:visual-team | critique appended to the active spec (else the brief) | advisory (normal/full) |
| Prototype (opt-in) | /kit:prototype | validated decision folded into the brief/spec + `prototype/<name>` branch pointer on the owning row | advisory (HITL; SPEC-206) |
| UI design (opt-in, downstream) | /kit:ui-design | brief -> generate (frontend-design) -> critique -> revise | advisory (downstream only) |
| Spec     | /kit:spec | spec exists, Status: DRAFT | spec-drift-guard hook |
| Validate | /kit:spec-validate | Status: VALIDATED | advisory (full lane) |
| Test plan (default for normal/full) | /kit:test-plan | `## Test plan` written into the spec, in the type's dialect (test-design-standard §5b) | advisory default (normal/full); tiny exempt |
| Build    | /kit:execute or /kit:next | tasks checked, verifier PASS | verification pipeline (worker, verifier, fix; max 2) |
| Review   | /kit:review or /kit:review-team | review verdict recorded | advisory |
| Docs     | /kit:docs | README/CHANGELOG match code | advisory |
| Ship     | /kit:ship | tagged + PR | ship gate (blocks on DO NOT SHIP), push-to-main blocker |
| Reflect  | /kit:retro | docs/retro/v<version>.md written | advisory |
| Debug (off-cycle) | /kit:debug | root cause recorded, fix verified, human-confirmed | iron law + guess-fix guard (anti-rationalization) |

Throughout: safety-gate blocks destructive Bash; anti-rationalization blocks
premature "done"; auto-format runs on edit; session-state-save and
post-compact-reinject protect long sessions. The Debug row is an off-cycle
entry point (a bug-lane loop), not a linear phase between Reflect and the next cycle.

## The V-model lens

> The ASCII V below is the canonical rendering. For a rendered vector version, see
> [`docs/v-model.svg`](docs/v-model.svg). (The README hero is a 6-phase mermaid lifecycle, the
> 10-second view; this section + the SVG are the full V.)

The cycle table above is the canonical phase list. This section reads it as a **V**.
The **left arm BUILDS**: each phase produces an artifact and statically reviews it
(verification, "did we build this right?"). The **right arm TESTS**: it executes the
test that validates each artifact and reports (validation, "does it actually work?").
**Build** is the vertex. The V-model's core move is that every artifact gets *two*
checks: a static review when it is produced (left/vertex) and a dynamic test later
(right). The kit does not shift test design up the left arm (it has one late
`/kit:test-plan` step), so the test-design + execution wing sits on the right.

```
   LEFT · BUILD (produce + review each artifact)        RIGHT · TEST (execute the mirror)
   ============================================        =================================

   Brief / Requirement ............................... Acceptance test   acceptance-verifier · /kit:verify
   build /kit:think · /kit:assign  · review brief-reviewer (/kit:think)
    Solution-design .................................. System test       system-verifier · /kit:verify
